resources.allowTrivial: Held on purpose, and the reason this scenario exists. The wind runs out at 45 s with no input, so the long warmup ends the run before the baseline is taken: the harness reports this row as already satisfied, which is the proof that every sample below is observed after gameplay stopped. A run that were still sailing here would be measuring the case playtests/float.playtest.json already covers.

The other half of the same precondition: the wind is spent before the first observation and cannot come back, so no step below can re-enter the sailing branch and quietly restore the updates this scenario is checking for.

components.allowTrivial: The finding. The ship samples the swell only when its visual update runs; while that update lived inside gameplay it stopped the moment the run ended, and this height froze at whatever wave the boat died on. Every sample here is post-terminal, so a seaHeight that no longer moves is the freeze itself rather than a still ocean.
The sea must still be simulating after the run is over. Without this row a frozen hull on a frozen ocean would satisfy floatGap, and the scenario would report green on a still photograph.
The drawn hull's design waterline still sits on the sea after the run is over; a finished game that leaves the boat hanging off its own surface is the visible half of the same defect.
A negative age means the GPU height copy never landed, so nothing downstream of it can be trusted.
